image_caption: ABSTRACT: The vast majority of transition metal (TM) catalyzed borylative transformations rely on $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \operatorname { s p } ^ { 2 } )$ complexes. Contrastingly, the chemistry $\operatorname { o f } { \dot { \mathrm { T M } } } \mathrm { - B } ( \operatorname { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ species and their potential in catalytic borylation remain surprisingly underdeveloped, due probably to the lack of suitable $\mathsf { b o r o n } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ reagents. Herein, we employ our recently developed $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { - } \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent to successfully enable a copper-catalyzed hydroboration of allenes for $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ bond formation. A comprehensive mechanistic study, including the isolation and structural characterization of $\texttt { a } \mathrm { C u - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ complex, substantiates the presence of a $\mathrm { C u - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ intermediate in the catalytic cycle.

Among these methods, C−B bond formation reactions, which ofer a straightforward strategy for directly introducing boron into organic molecules, have been extensively studied over the past decades and led to considerable progress.<sup>4,5</sup> Among all the achievements, transition-metal (TM) catalysis has proved to be one of the irreplaceable strategies due to its versatility in diferent reaction modes, broad substrate compatibility, and excellent selectivity control.<sup>5</sup> This has facilitated the eficient creation of organoboron compounds with diverse structures, thereby enriching the library of organoborons with potential functionalities.

Nevertheless, compared to the extensive reports on $\mathrm { C } -$ $\mathrm { B } \left( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 2 } \right)$ bond formation, transition-metal-catalyzed borylation for the direct incorporation of an $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ boron moiety into organic molecules is less explored. On the other hand, as the result of $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ bond construction, four-coordinate organoborons are expected to have better air and moisture stability than their three-coordinate counterparts.<sup>6</sup> For example, some $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } )$ species, such as C2-borylated pyridines and acylboranes,<sup>7</sup> still face stability issues and are often structurally identified by masking with N-methyliminodiacetic acid (MIDA) or converting to borate salts, where the boron center is four-coordinated.<sup>8</sup>

text: are well-documented as key intermediates in some $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } )$ bond construction reactions. $\mathrm { 9 g - m }$ In contrast, the generation or detection of $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ complexes in borylation reactions remains elusive.<sup>10</sup> The lack of an empty p orbital on $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ boron reduces the potential for π-back bonding from metal to boron, leading to a relatively weak $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ bond.<sup>11</sup> Additionally, suitable boron reagents or precursors for the generation of versatile $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ species are scarce.

Weller’s early research provides an example of Rh-catalyzed hydroboration of tert-butyl ethene by amine-boranes (Scheme $1 \mathrm { \dot { a } } ) . ^ { 1 2 }$ Although further evidence for Rh−B bond formation is needed, this seminal work supports the theoretical basis for four-coordinate organoboron preparation via metal catalysis.<sup>13</sup> Later, the Curran group and the Zhu and Zhou group independently pioneered the transition-metal-catalyzed carbene insertion into B−H bonds of Lewis base-coordinated boranes (Scheme 1b).<sup>14</sup> Although a $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ intermediate is not present in the reaction pathway, the research sparks interest in using this approach for $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ bond construction.<sup>15</sup> However, the requirement for diazo compounds or other carbene precursors limits the method’s applicability to other types of organic molecules.

Considering the established methods of producing TM− $\mathrm { B } \big ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 2 } \big )$ species from diboron reagents such as bis(pinacolato)- diboron $\mathrm { \bar { ( B _ { 2 } p i n _ { 2 } ) } } .$ , we propose employing the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { - } \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent as the $\bar { \mathrm { T M } } { - } \mathrm { B } \bar { ( } \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } \bar { ) }$ precursor. Among the reported $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } -$ $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent, only Santos’ reagent $\mathrm { \Delta P D I P A } ^ { \mathrm { \prime } _ { \mathrm { 1 6 } } }$ and its derivative<sup>17</sup> have been used in transition-metal catalysis as a borylation agent. However, this approach results in the formation of a $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \operatorname { s p } ^ { 2 } )$ intermediate, with the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ boryl being sacrificed during the transmetalation process. Recently, we reported a neutral $\mathsf { \bar { s p } } ^ { 2 } \mathrm { - } \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent, (I<sup>i</sup>Pr)BH Bpin. This reagent exhibits unique electronic and steric properties and distinct reactivities compared to existing boron reagents. 18 Here, we initiate research on exploring the potential of this neutral $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathsf { - s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent as a precursor of $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ species, as well as its efects on the reactivity and selectivity in transition-metal-catalyzed $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ formation reactions (Scheme 1c). After many attempts, a copper-catalyzed hydroboration of allenes with an $\mathsf { s p } ^ { \hat { 2 } } \mathrm { - } \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent has been achieved. More importantly, the successful isolation and structural characterization of a $\mathrm { { \dot { T } M - B } } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ complex evidence a new potential pathway for transition-metal-catalyzed $\mathrm { C } -$ $\mathsf { B } \big ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } \big )$ formation reactions. The detailed experimental results are compiled in this communication.

To investigate the reactivity and selectivity of the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathsf { - s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagents in transition-metal catalysis, we conducted its reactions with allenes, which are known for their challenging regioselectivity control in hydroboration reactions.<sup>19</sup> The reaction of $\mathrm { { \dot { s p } } } ^ { 2 } { \cdot } \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagents 2 with 1-phenyl-3- phenethyl-disubstituted allene 1a using copper catalysis was studied. Diferent diboron reagents 2a-2d with various NHCs (NHC = N-heterocyclic carbene) on the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ boron were evaluated (Scheme 2a). Under optimal reaction conditions (for detailed condition screening, see the Supporting Information, Table S1), the reaction of allene 1a with (I<sup>i</sup>Pr)BH Bpin 2c aforded vinyl borane Z-3c in 84% <sup>1</sup>H NMR yield, along with 11% stereoisomer E-3c, resulting in a

Interestingly, in the reaction with diboron 2b, where the R group on NHC was a cyclohexyl group, another regioisomer 4b was observed alongside expected Z-3b and E-3b. Although further studies are ongoing to understand this unexpected phenomenon, the above results suggest that modifying the structure of the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathsf { - s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent can significantly influence the reactivity and selectivity.

Later, we found that replacing the alkyl group on the allene with a bulkier cyclohexyl group improved the Z/E selectivity to ${ > } 2 0 / 1$ (Scheme 2b). Control experiments proved the crucial role of the copper catalyst, the base NaO<sup>t</sup>Bu, and <sup>t</sup>BuOH. Screening of other ligands did not further promote the eficiency and selectivity (Table S3). These results suggest that in addition to the structures of both the allene substrates and boron reagents, the ligands on the metal catalyst also play a role in determining the reaction eficiency and selectivity.

As shown in Scheme 3a, 5 features a nearly square-planar, centro-symmetric, eightmembered $\mathrm { ( C u B ) _ { 4 } }$ ring, with $\mathrm { B - C u - B }$ angle of $1 5 8 . 0 4 ( ^ { \circ } ) ^ { \circ }$ NMR data confirmed the presence of two hydrogen atoms on the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ boron center. Subsequently, a stoichiometric reaction of complex 5 with allene 1b was carried out in the presence of IMes ligand (Scheme 3c). The borylation products Z-6 and E-6 were obtained in 10% and 4% yields, respectively. The decreased yield and stereoselectivity were likely attributed to the poor stability and solubility of complex 5. When complex 5 was used as the catalyst, along with 10 mol % IMes, the reaction of 1b with diboron 2e underwent smoothly to form Z-6 in 82% yield with a Z/E ratio of 96/4 (Scheme 3d). These results support the involvement of a $\mathrm { C u } { \mathrm { - } } \mathrm { B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ intermediate in the reaction pathway.

A proposed catalytic cycle is illustrated in Scheme 3f $\left( \mathrm { L } _ { \mathrm { M } } = \right.$ ligand on metal; $\mathrm { L _ { B } } = \mathrm { l i g a n d }$ on boron). Transmetalation of $\mathrm { L } _ { \mathrm { M } } \mathrm { C u O }$ <sup>t</sup>Bu with $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathsf { - s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron initially generates $\mathrm { C u } { - } \mathrm { B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ intermediate IM1. Then the allene undergoes Cu−B bond insertion to form borylcupration intermediate IM2. Finally, $\gamma \mathrm { - }$ protonation of IM2 produces the desired vinyl borane and regenerates the $\mathrm { { C u } ( I ) }$ catalyst. To verify the protonation step, a deuterium experiment was performed using $d _ { 4 } .$ methanol as the proton source, resulting in Z-3e-D in 16% yield and 80% deuterium incorporation at the benzylic position (Scheme 3e).

The −Br group led to a decrease in both yield and selectivity (Z-3j). Substituents, such as trifluoromethyl (Z-3l to ${ \cal Z } { \cdot } 3 { \bf n } )$ , alkyls $\left( Z { \cdot } 3 p , \ Z { \cdot } 3 { \bf q } , \ Z { \cdot } 3 { \bf u } \right)$ , biphenyl (Z-3r), trifluoromethoxy $\left( Z { \cdot } 3 \mathbf { s } \right)$ , and benzodioxane (Z-3t), were wellcompatiable, afording the desired vinyl boranes in Z/E selectivity larger than 95/5. Slightly decreased selectivity was observed when allenes with electron-donating methoxy groups were used (Z-3o, Z-3v). Both ester and amide groups were tolerated while providing a low yield (Z-3w) or compromised selectivity (Z-3x). In addition, naphthalene- and phenanthrene-derived vinyl boranes $Z \mathbf { - } 3 \mathbf { y }$ and Z-3z were synthesized in 66% and 79% yields, respectively. Besides, heterocycles, such as pyridine (Z-3aa), quinoline (Z-3ab), thiophene $\left( Z { - } 3 { \mathsf { a c } } \right) _ { i }$ benzothiophene (Z-3ad), and carbazole (Z-3ae), were also tolerated with this Cu-catalyzed hydroboration. Additionally, compound Z-3af, derived from drug molecule adapalene, was successfully prepared in 62% yield.

Allenes with various alkyl substituents were also tested. In general, branched alkyls such as <sup>i</sup>Pr and <sup>t</sup>Bu performed better than linear groups (Z-3ag and Z-3ah versus $Z – 3 c$ and Z-3ai) in eficiency and selectivity. Vinyl boranes bearing cycloalkyl groups with diferent ring sizes (Z-3aj to Z-3al) were prepared under the standard conditions. In addition, the piperidine group was well-tolerated, yielding Z-3am stereoselectively. Furthermore, complex substrates derived from drug molecules naproxen and gemfibrozil as well as natural products dehydroabietic acid and lithocholic acid reacted well with 2c to aford derivatives Z-3an to Z-3aq containing the $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ moiety.

It is noteworthy that when using allene 1b with a bulkier cyclohexyl group as the substrate, diboron reagents 2 with various NHC ligands all provided corresponding borylation products with approximately 95/5 Z/E-selectivity (Z-6, Z-3ar, and Z-3as), further highlighting the influence of substrates’ structure on the reaction selectivity (3ar vs 3a, 3as vs 3d). The reaction of 1,3-diphenyl-allene resulted in a diferent selectivity, providing vinyl borane E-3at as the main product.

The newly formed $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ bond in vinyl borane Z-3e underwent further transformations, allowing for the introduction of diverse functional groups including ketones (7), aryls (10), and azides (11). The NHC boryl group in compound Z-3e was readily converted into a more reactive $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 }$ boronic ester (9) through a reaction with NCS (N-chlorosuccinimide) followed by hydrolysis. When HCl was used in place of NCS, reduction of compound Z-3e occurred, resulting in the formation of alkyl boronic ester 8 in a high yield (Scheme 4a). This reduction is proposed to proceed via alkene protonation, followed $\boldsymbol { \mathrm { b y } }$ a hydride shift (see Supporting Information for the proposed mechanism), which is supported by deuterium labeling experiments (Scheme 4a, bottom). Furthermore, hydroboration of vinyl borane E-3at led to the introduction of an $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 }$ boryl group, afording the diborylalkanes 12 and $_ { 1 2 } \cdot$ as two regioisomers (Scheme 4b). Additionally, the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }$ boryl can undergo further transformations based on the B− H bond. As shown in Scheme 4c, an eficient hydroboration of styrene using ${ \cal Z } { \cdot } 3 { \bf q }$ and $Z \mathbf { - } 3 \mathbf { e }$ led to the synthesis of difunctionalized four-coordinate boranes 13 and 14, respectively. More importantly, 14 was proved to undergo a Zweifeltype reaction,<sup>25</sup> afording the formal intramolecular C−C bond formation product 15 in 55% yield. This highlights a useful transformation that is not achievable with the Bpin analogues.

In summary, the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathsf { - s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent (NHC)BH Bpin has been demonstrated as an $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 } .$ -borylation agent in transitionmetal catalysis for the first time. It enables the formation of an unprecedented $\mathrm { C u } { - } \mathrm { B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ tetrameric species featuring the Cu−B−Cu three-center-two-electron bonds, paving a versatile avenue to $\mathrm { C - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ bond construction and four-coordinate organoboron compound synthesis. Detailed mechanistic studies and DFT calculations are currently underway to gain deeper insight into the selectivity control of $\mathrm { T M - B } ( \mathrm { s p } ^ { 3 } )$ species involved in borylation reactions. Further application of the $\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 } \mathsf { - s p } ^ { 3 }$ diboron reagent in the borylation of diverse organic molecules and the efects of its structure on reactivity and selectivity are under investigation in our group.
